observations: body L1-L2: the label «(β)» stands at the margin and the formula is centred where it is printed. Formula (β) gives the distance only if ψ is read as the anomaly less 90°, as in al-Battānī's rule (p. 78, L20-L24: «de eo 90° deme»); with ψ the anomaly itself, as defined on p. 253, (α) holds for every anomaly, √((60ᵖ + e cos ψ/R)² + (e sin ψ/R)²). For e = 5ᵖ 15′ and an anomaly of 120°, (α) and (β) with ψ = 30° both give 57ᵖ 33′; (β) with ψ = 120° would give 55ᵖ 31′.

body L3-L11: the figure stands on the left of these lines and is redrawn from the print: the epicycle about A (radius 24.7 pt), the line from its top H through M and A to F and the Earth E, the line from G to E, the radius AG and the perpendicular MG (89.97° to HE), with the bold italic letters where they are printed. It is not to scale: AE is 4.3 radii of the epicycle, against 60ᵖ : 5ᵖ 15′ = 11.4.
body L6-L11: in the right triangle EMG, EG² = EM² + MG² with EM = AE + AM; AM and MG are the cosine and the sine of the anomaly HAG in the epicycle of radius AG = e; with AE = 60ᵖ this is (α).

body L12-L18: heavy brackets open and close Schiaparelli's addition; «lineis 25–26» (long dash, 5.5 pt) are p. 78, L25-L26, «de singulis huius distantiae gradibus minutum deme». A minute for each degree is 1/60 of the distance, one part when the distance is 60 parts; Schiaparelli would subtract the one part of the radius of the Earth. The dash before «Schiaparelli» measures 10.2 pt.

body L19: the dash after «e)» measures 10.2 pt, that of «27–29» 5.4 pt; the lines cited are p. 78, L27-L29, «sume productum minutorum quartae columnae in quintam columnam tabularum aequationis Lunae».

body L20-L32: the figure stands on the right of these lines and is redrawn from the print: the circle about the Earth E (radius 90.2 pt) and the eccentric about F (radius 60.8 pt), their left halves from the line A F E, touching at A; the line from A through F and E; the epicycle about N (radius 19.6 pt), whose centre lies on the eccentric (0.1 pt off); the tangent EK, drawn on beyond K (N stands 19.8 pt from it); the lines EG and E N H; the radii NK and NG; the perpendicular GM (87.6° to NH); the bold italic letters where they are printed. The N below the centre of the epicycle is broken. As drawn, the angle NEK is 26.8° and EF : FA is 27.2 : 60.8.

body L22-L29: «al–Battānī» has a long dash (5.4 pt). The fifth column of al-Battānī's tables of the Moon (Part II, p. 78-81), the increment of the equation, reaches 2° 40′ at its greatest, Schiaparelli's number (7° 40′ − 5° 1′ = 2° 39′). In L29 no dash stands before «Schiaparelli»; a speck over its E is not transcribed, and a heavy bracket closes the addition.
body L30: the head stands beside the figure but is centred on the measure, as printed; the dash after «f)» measures 10.1 pt, that of «31–32» 5.4 pt.

body L33-L40: a heavy bracket opens Schiaparelli's addition, which goes on to p. 255. The «verba Italicis litteris impressa» are p. 78, L31-L32: «eo utere ut supra iis 5ᵖ ¼; invenies hypotenusam Lunae aequatam ad declivitatem epicycli»; NK = 5ᵖ 15′ is that 5ᵖ ¼. The dash before «Cognito» measures 10.4 pt; «(v. adn. d)» is note d) of p. 253.
